coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Private employers register each worker in EMTA's Töötamise register (TÖR) and file TSD by the 10th via free e-MTA; SMS/phone shortcut exists (emta.ee/eraklient/e-teenused-maksutarkus/registrid-paringud/eraisikust-tooandja). Free state tool covers it; no sector-specific duty found.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No 2026 source found. Only old material: Waste Act s.105 limits on buying cables, waste permit for metal waste collection. Nothing new beyond general waste-permit regime (see K06).

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Pawnbrokers and traders are AML obliged persons under RahaPTS, supervised by RAB; RAB 2025 feedback (fiu.ee 2026-03) says reporting activity is very low (2 reports in 2025) and the EU AMLR drops general traders from the obliged list, keeping precious metals/stones/high-value goods. Small buyer group; no software gap proven.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: 88 holders of RAB precious-metal/stone buying and wholesale licence at end 2025, no new licences issued; VMTS amendment in force 1 July 2025 moved maker's-mark registration to an electronic register run under ministerial regulation (draft Sept 2025). Small, shrinking group.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: About 150 licensed lammutuskoda; only they can deregister vehicles; dismantling certificate must be free; drafts add producer-contract requirement and 2027 state-fee deregistration route. Sources are partly old or draft; status of drafts unverified.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Animal keepers report to the PRIA/PTA agricultural animals register (free e-PRIA). Nothing specific on dealers or transport found.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Nothing found for small abattoirs or butchers in the single search; only general PTA food-business self-control (omakontroll) guidance. Not enough to judge.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: All apiaries must be in PRIA's agricultural animals register; monthly colony-number reporting via e-PRIA service (Minister of Rural Affairs reg. no. 74); bee-colony support (TARU) deadlines 30 Apr / 5 May / 15 June. About 46,685 colonies registered at 30.04.2024. Free e-PRIA covers it; hobbyist buyers.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Vets report prescribed/used medicines to PTA via client portal (Oct and 5 January cycle, per 2022 regulation, EU 2021/578 art.15 animal categories). Nothing new beyond K01.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Groundwater abstraction needs a Keskkonnaamet permit with annual/quarterly volume limits, monthly meter readings, 5-yearly level measurement; hydrogeological work needs a licensed firm; Water Act amendment in the Riigikogu. Permit holders are mostly larger users.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K03 and K06.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Two searches-worth of results gave only the Equipment Safety Act (SeOS) framework, a 2026 draft changing TTJA's supervision information system, and the Transpordiamet check of crane/lift audits on vehicles. Owner inspection duties not confirmed; unverified.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: 973 systems under Terviseamet supervision in 2025 (52 fewer than 2024); new Directive 2020/2184 indicators (PFAS, uranium, chlorate, microcystin-LR, Legionella) had to be monitored by 12.01.2026. Private wells are outside supervision. Operators are mostly utilities and housing associations.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Draft regulation of 27 April 2026 sets training programme/exam for professional users, distributors and advisers under the amended Plant Protection Act, including record-keeping of products used. Adoption and in-force date not confirmed.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Agency labour/recruitment needs a business-activity notice in MTR; Tööinspektsioon ran a 2024 targeted inspection of labour-hire firms (rest periods, contract type). No user-company report form found.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: New cemetery law shelved (ERR 2025/26 piece); Kalmistuseadus unchanged since 2023; some municipalities use the HAUDI cemetery register. Nothing new for funeral firms.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: MTÜs file annual reports and beneficial-owner data to the e-Business Register (free portal); no 2026 change found for congregations or religious associations. Halal/kosher: nothing found.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Bill 725 SE (planned in force 1 Jan 2026) centralises taxi-driver service cards (teenindajakaart) in the public transport register, drops the photo, adds B1 Estonian proof; taximeter, roof light, price list and printer required unless booked via app. Adoption status not confirmed.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Currency exchange needs RAB or Finantsinspektsioon licence; RAB issued a guidance letter to currency exchange providers on 30.06.2026 (text unreadable via fetch). Nothing found on market or street traders.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Childminders: licence transition to Basic Education Act (EHIS) or Social Welfare Act basis, notify by 1 Dec 2025, SHS compliance by 31 Aug 2026, unconverted licences void from 1 Sept 2026. Small non-animal primary producers: threshold rule due 1 July 2026 is being rewritten (ERR 30.06.2026). Commercial cat/dog breeders must be in PRIA register since 2021. Hunting: JAHIS reporting by hunting-area users. Tattoo studios and driving schools: not searched.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: New Security Activities Act in force 1 July 2024 (activity-based licences, staff vocational qualification and language requirements); Labour Inspectorate 2024 targeted inspection of temp-work agencies. No software gap confirmed. Weak candidate.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers
coverage.found: Construction supply-chain/attendance is K04/K07 (known). Quarry and sand/gravel pit holders file a mining-volume report plus mining-right fee declaration quarterly by the 17th via KOTKAS, even for nil quarters, with markscheider survey data; Keskkonnaamet guidance Dec 2025. New candidate.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: RahaPTS applies to all brokers regardless of size; FIU (RAB) is supervising real estate firms (2025 correspondence with a broker found). No size-based relief found. AML-kit candidate, generic risk.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: MKM pre-draft (VTK) of 10.06.2026 'Turismiseaduse muutmine lühiajalise üüri turu korrastamiseks', consultation to 1 Sep 2026; hotel and tourism associations demand a state register and a 60-day / unit-count threshold, and the VTK itself declined a register. Electronic guest-registration database plan was paused earlier. Candidate.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: EUDR applies from 30 Dec 2026 (micro/small operators to 30 Jun 2027 per a FedEx Estonia page; verify against official text); Kliimaministeerium presentation of 19.03.2026 says forest owners and cattle farmers must be able to evidence non-deforestation, downstream traders must collect and keep declaration numbers 5 years. Fish logbooks are K09 (rejected). Candidate.

coverage.category: 31. Apartment associations (korteriühistu)
coverage.found: Very large quiet group (annual report, billing, heat-cost allocation). One search found no specific 2026 duty or dedicated product pricing; only theses on KÜ accounting systems. Left unverified.

coverage.category: 32. F-gas (FOKA) equipment owners and refrigeration/HVAC service firms
coverage.found: Keskkonnaamet FOKA register (page updated 25.06.2026): equipment registered by CO2-equivalent; only permit holders may service; maintenance logs / leak checks tied to Reg (EU) 2024/573; Kliimaministeerium sent a draft regulation on 12.03.2026 changing the handling-permit and register statute; drafts mention registration within two weeks of installation (unconfirmed adopted). No third-party technician software found.

coverage.category: 33. Radiation-licensed small clinics (dental X-ray, veterinary X-ray)
coverage.found: Dental intraoral X-ray is a registration (200 EUR) under energy and climate minister regulation No 41 of 18.07.2025 via KOTKAS; QA tests every 3 years (intraoral) and 2 years (extraoral). One-off-ish duty, low frequency.

coverage.category: 34. Alcohol and tobacco retail (MTR activity register, Alcohol Register)
coverage.found: Alcohol sold only from MTR-registered premises, e-shop sales count as retail. Drafts: abolish State Alcohol Register (Feb 2026), restrict storage to registered premises and require age verification for e-commerce (Nov 2025); status unconfirmed. Tobacco traceability and retail rules not found. Burden is falling, weak.

coverage.category: 35. Taxi and ride-hailing (teenindajakaart, taximeter)
coverage.found: Bill 725 SE (consolidate taxi service-card records into one register, proposed in force 1 Jan 2026) and bill 578 SE (B1 Estonian proof, taximeter price rules); outcome unconfirmed. Overlaps group A cat. 18.

coverage.category: 36. Forest owners (metsateatis, Metsaregister)
coverage.found: Owners file forest notices (metsateatis) via ID-card login in Metsaregister, checked against about 80 data layers; no tool linking it to EUDR evidence found. Merged into the EUDR candidate.

result.competitor: No Estonia-specific guest-register product found. Generic channel managers and PMS tools (Smoobu from 28 EUR/month, Airbnb channel-manager partners such as Guesty and SiteMinder) offer online check-in. Chekin's police-reporting country list does not include Estonia. There is no state portal: the e-guest database was paused in 2020, and the State Chancellery's e-accommodation card project dates from 2019. Estonian PMS vendors were not checked.
result.duty: Current: TurS § 24 requires accommodation providers to register guests on a visitor card (külastajakaart) and keep the cards 2 years. Electronic registration is optional since the 2020-21 amendment. Penalty not verified. Proposed: the MKM VTK of 10.06.2026 would clarify that platform short-term rentals are an accommodation service and that the Schengen guest-registration duty covers them. The tourism sector wants a national register (EU Reg 2024/1028 applies from 20 May 2026). The VTK has not been turned into a bill yet, and MKM targets entry into force in 2027-28. The Riigi Teataja consolidated text could not be read (the fetch returned an empty page), so § 24's current wording was confirmed only from secondary sources.
result.market: Tallinn had about 1,322 (BnBCalc, Airbnb and VRBO only) to 3,558 (AirDNA, June 2026) active short-term rental listings, about 76% professionally managed. The sector's joint opinion (as summarised in the claim; I did not open it) gives a 2025 market of 103.9M EUR, 86% of income from legal persons and 72% of providers running one unit. No national count of hosts was found.
result.reason: Today's duty is light. Under the Tourism Act (TurS) § 24, as cited by ERR and Riigikogu sources, hosts register guests on a visitor card and keep it for 2 years. Electronic registration is optional and there is no routine reporting to the police. The state guest e-database was paused. The new short-term rental regime is still only a June 2026 policy proposal (VTK). Consultation closed 1 Sep 2026, no bill was found, and MKM targets 2027-28. Whether there will be a register, thresholds or registration numbers is undecided, so the core duty can't yet be specified. Generic tools (Smoobu, channel managers, PMS online check-in) already cover the card replacement. Chekin does not list Estonia. The market is small: roughly 1,300-3,600 Tallinn listings, mostly managed by companies. Revisit when a bill appears.

result.competitor: Free state FOKA portal (foka.envir.ee) for registration and maintenance entries; I found no mobile, X-road push or bulk upload. International refrigerant/CMMS tools with leak-check scheduling and F-gas logs: Parasense, Fabrico, GoCanvas F-Gas Log Sheet. I found no Estonian-language tool or one integrated with FOKA.
result.duty: EU F-gas Reg 2024/573 (directly applicable): equipment holding 5 t CO2e or more needs periodic leak checks and records kept for 5 years. Estonian Atmospheric Air Protection Act (AÕKS) plus FOKA register statute: equipment and servicing must be registered in FOKA via foka.envir.ee, and servicing is limited to Keskkonnaamet handling-permit holders. The authority consolidating handling data reports by 20 June each year. A 2025 draft amendment to the AÕKS (KeMÜ) would extend registration to all equipment of 5 t CO2e or more, and a Kliimaministeerium draft of 12.03.2026 amends the permit and FOKA statute; adoption of both is unconfirmed. I did not find the Estonian fine amounts. A 2022 amendment raised fine rates, but I did not confirm the figures.
result.market: Not quantified. I found no count of handling-permit holders or registered equipment; Keskkonnaamet or Eesti Külmaliit would have it. Likely only a few hundred service firms in Estonia, plus shops and restaurants that own the equipment, who rely on those firms for the records.
result.reason: The duty is real. Reg (EU) 2024/573 applies directly in Estonia. Under it, operators of equipment holding 5 t CO2e or more must have periodic leak checks and keep records for 5 years. Equipment and servicing must be entered in the Keskkonnaamet FOKA register (foka.envir.ee), and only permit holders may do the servicing. I did not verify the Estonian fines, leak-check intervals, or whether the 12.03.2026 draft (which may extend registration) was adopted. I found no Estonian or FOKA-integrated tool. Foreign tools (Parasense, Fabrico, GoCanvas F-gas log) already handle leak-check scheduling and logbooks, though, and the FOKA portal is free. The buyer pool is small and unquantified, perhaps a few hundred permit holders (I found no register count). Willingness to pay and market size are weak.

result.competitor: Generic timber EUDR platforms do the core job (geolocation, risk assessment, DDS filing): cubemos, osapiens, VERSO, Tanso, Coolset, TraceX and PEFC TimberID. ERP modules also exist (acadon for Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, OPTI-NET). Large buyers such as Metsä Group issue EUDR reference and verification numbers for their customers and can act as representatives. The EU information system itself is free. Not found: any Estonian-language tool linked to Metsaregister or metsateatis, any state-provided geolocation service, or any EUDR offering from Erametsaliit or the forest owner co-operatives (metsaühistud). This gap is unverified, not confirmed.
result.duty: Confirmed and directly applicable EU law: Reg. (EU) 2023/1115 as amended by Reg. (EU) 2025/2650. The company or person that first places wood on the market, or exports it, must do due diligence and file a due diligence declaration (DDS, "HTD" in Estonian) in the EU information system. Downstream businesses keep the DDS numbers for 5 years. Dates: 30 Dec 2026 for medium and large firms and for timber-sector micro and small firms. 30 Jun 2027 applies only to non-timber micro and small firms, so the claim's date is wrong for timber. The Commission's May 2026 review confirmed no further delay, and the July 2026 product-scope act removed cattle hides and leather. Micro and small primary operators in low-risk countries file a one-time simplified declaration instead of a DDS per shipment. Keskkonnaamet (KeA) is named as the supervising authority in the 19.03.2026 briefing. Estonian penalty amounts: not reached.
result.market: Not reached. I found no register count of Estonian forest owners, sawmills or timber traders in scope. The size of the private forest owner population and the number of sawmills were not verified in this session.
result.reason: The duty is real. EUDR (Reg. 2023/1115, amended by Reg. 2025/2650) applies directly in Estonia, and the Climate Ministry and Keskkonnaamet briefing of 19.03.2026 confirms it. However, the claim's dates are partly wrong: timber micro and small firms must comply from 30 Dec 2026 and do not get the 30 Jun 2027 extension. Small Estonian forest owners selling their own timber count as micro/small primary operators in a low-risk country, so they only file a one-time simplified declaration. That leaves little recurring pain. Sawmills and traders mostly collect reference numbers. Several timber EUDR platforms (osapiens, VERSO, Tanso, cubemos, TimberID) and big buyers such as Metsä Group already handle filing and reference numbers. The only gap found is a tool in Estonian that pulls plot data from the forest register (unverified).

The licence duty exists, but it sits in the Alusharidusseadus (AHS, in force 1 Sept 2025), not the Basic Education Act as the claim says. SKA letters say old SHS licences stayed valid to 1 Sept 2026 or until an AHS § 43 licence is granted. Today is 9 Oct 2026, so the one-off deadline has passed. Only a small residue remains, and no recurring filing was found. Market is tiny: a 2017 Terviseamet survey implies about 260 providers (my arithmetic, nearly a decade old). The state registers (MTR, EHIS) already handle the licence. I found no dedicated childminder compliance software, but the buyer pool is too small and the trigger is gone. Not checked: current AHS text on Riigi Teataja, and the official SKA page.

Duty status is unconfirmed. Sources are only drafts, a Feb 2024 ERR plan and Riigikogu texts. I found no evidence the bill was adopted or took effect. The 1 Nov 2026 and 800 EUR dates come from drafts. A baseline duty exists: licensed dismantlers must send dismantled-vehicle data electronically to Transpordiamet via the liiklusregister e-services, under a data-processing agreement (HR Auto OÜ example). That flow is state-provided. I saw no dismantler software, but the market is only about 150 firms, so willingness to pay is low. Producer-contract and deregistration changes mostly shift cost to producers and the state. Recurring paperwork is small. Not verified: Riigi Teataja consolidated text, any vendor, the register count.

Duty is real: the operator must agree a multi-year drinking-water control plan (kontrollkava) with Terviseamet under Social Minister regulation no 61 of 24.09.2019 (§11), and Terviseamet letters list new parameters (PFAS, uranium, chlorate, microcystin-LR, Legionella) due by 12.01.2026. The cycle is multi-year, so frequency is low. Small systems often sample only once a year to once every 10 years, and labs do the sampling. Roughly 1105 systems were supervised in 2023, 807 of them designated utilities; 973 in 2025 per the claim. The market is small and fragmented, and each plan is a small recurring task, so willingness to pay is weak. I found no dedicated software, but I ran few searches. Penalties were not checked and the 2026 amendments were not read. Not rejected, but weak.

result.reason: Duty looks real: the Riigi Teataja regulation (KKM m22, as amended by m48) requires a mining volume report with the fee declaration by the 17th of the month after each quarter, even with nil extraction. Records are kept 7 years after the permit expires. Survey frequency depends on annual volume: quarterly above 200,000 units, yearly at 50,000-200,000. I could not confirm that KOTKAS is the submission channel. The Keskkonnaamet PDF was unreadable. No permit-holder count was found. No Estonian competitor was found, but I did not search deeply. Small pits are few, volumes are low, and surveyors may already file for clients. This is a niche with a small market and a free state channel.

Duty is real: KÜ keep accounts and file an annual report to the commercial register within 6 months of year end (deadline 30.06 for the 2025 report, from an ariregister entry). Associations of 10 or fewer apartments with no board are exempt. Only an old ERR article gives a count (over 22,000 KÜ), so the market is large but the figure is dated. I did not verify the statute text. Competition is not cleared: Excellent has a KÜ module, and Estonian KÜ-specific vendors were not surfaced, so I could not verify them. KÜ pay accountants or managers, so buyers are fragmented and willingness to pay is modest. Generic billing and accounting are out of scope. The claim is too broad and mostly overlaps existing tools. A narrow angle (the annual report's per-apartment cost table, or an inspections calendar) is untested.

The duty is real. Under RahaPTS, real estate intermediaries must have a risk assessment, internal rules, due diligence and beneficial-owner identification, and must report suspicious transactions to the FIU (RAB). RAB supervises them on a risk basis. The ERR 2019 article and RAB's 2025 feedback and letters show the sector is active. The duty is ongoing rather than periodic, so frequency is low. Penalties were not found, and I could not read the 2025 feedback PDF. Competitors: no broker-specific Estonian tool turned up in two searches, but generic KYC and AML tools exist, and RAB publishes free guidance. Market size is not found; the sector is small and the state's own risk assessment says only 12 reports were filed in five years. Willingness to pay looks weak, so I score it 3. The EU AMLR from July 2027 may change scope.
